caption.en: The title page of J. M. Stoddart's authorized American vocal score (Philadelphia, copyright 1880), the song's earliest known printing, with the boxed notice in which Gilbert and Sullivan warn against "unauthorized editions".
caption.es: La portada de la partitura vocal estadounidense autorizada de J. M. Stoddart (Filadelfia, copyright de 1880), la primera impresión conocida de la canción, con el aviso enmarcado en el que Gilbert y Sullivan advierten contra las "unauthorized editions" (ediciones no autorizadas).

source: W. S. Gilbert and Arthur Sullivan, The Pirates of Penzance; or, The Slave of Duty, authorized copyright edition, vocal score (Philadelphia: J. M. Stoddart & Co., copyright 1880), title page (cropped below a later owner's handwritten inscription)

alt.en: A printed libretto page numbered 34. After the police's lines ending "Our obvious course Is now to hide." comes an italic stage direction in brackets, "Police conceal themselves in aisle L. ... They enter cautiously, and come down stage on tiptoe." Then "Chorus. Pirates." with "(Very loud.)" in the margin beside "With cat-like tread Upon our prey we steal", the police answering "(Pianissimo.) Tarantara! tarantara!", and the page running on to Samuel's "Here's your crowbar And your centre-bit" and "You may want to hit!"
alt.es: Página impresa de un libreto con el número 34. Tras los versos de los policías que terminan "Our obvious course Is now to hide." viene una acotación en cursiva entre paréntesis, "Police conceal themselves in aisle L. ... They enter cautiously, and come down stage on tiptoe." Luego "Chorus. Pirates." con "(Very loud.)" en el margen junto a "With cat-like tread Upon our prey we steal", los policías responden "(Pianissimo.) Tarantara! tarantara!", y la página sigue con el "Here's your crowbar And your centre-bit" de Samuel hasta "You may want to hit!"

caption.en: Page 34 of Hitchcock's New York libretto (undated, catalogued 1879), one of the first American libretti: beside the pirates' words about silence, the stage direction reads "(Very loud.)"
caption.es: La página 34 del libreto neoyorquino de Hitchcock (sin fecha, catalogado en 1879), uno de los primeros libretos estadounidenses: junto a las palabras de los piratas sobre el silencio, la acotación dice "(Very loud.)" (muy fuerte).

source: W. S. Gilbert and Arthur Sullivan, The Pirates of Penzance; or, The Slave of Duty, comic opera, complete libretto, authorized copyright edition (New York: Hitchcock Publishing Company, 49 Eighth Avenue, undated, catalogued 1879), p. 34

alt.en: A printed page of music, page 121, headed "No 12" and "Solo, Samuel, & Chorus of Pirates." with an italic stage direction across the top ending "The King is laden with burglarious tools and pistols, etc. etc." The piano is marked "Allegro marziale" with loud and soft chords; the pirates' line above has the words "With cat-like read up-on our prey we steal" (the t of "tread" missing in the print), the "Chorus of Police" comes in with "Ta-ran-ta-ra", and the last system has "So steal-thi-ly the Pi-rate creeps, While all the house-hold sound-ly sleeps."
alt.es: Página impresa de música, la 121, con el encabezado "No 12" y "Solo, Samuel, & Chorus of Pirates." y una acotación en cursiva en lo alto que termina "The King is laden with burglarious tools and pistols, etc. etc." El piano lleva la indicación "Allegro marziale" con acordes fuertes y suaves; la línea de los piratas, encima, tiene la letra "With cat-like read up-on our prey we steal" (a "tread" le falta la t en la impresión), el "Chorus of Police" entra con "Ta-ran-ta-ra", y el último sistema dice "So steal-thi-ly the Pi-rate creeps, While all the house-hold sound-ly sleeps."

caption.en: Act II, No. 12 begins on page 121 of Stoddart's 1880 vocal score: Sullivan's march, Allegro marziale, in D, under a stage direction that gives the Pirate King his "burglarious tools and pistols".
caption.es: El acto II, n.º 12, empieza en la página 121 de la partitura vocal de Stoddart de 1880: la marcha de Sullivan, Allegro marziale, en Re, bajo una acotación que da al rey pirata sus "burglarious tools and pistols" (herramientas de ladrón y pistolas).

source: W. S. Gilbert and Arthur Sullivan, The Pirates of Penzance; or, The Slave of Duty, authorized copyright edition, vocal score (Philadelphia: J. M. Stoddart & Co., copyright 1880), Act II, No. 12, p. 121

alt.en: A printed page of music numbered 152, with Chappell's plate number 23731 at the foot. Rehearsal letter E and "ff" mark both vocal lines: the upper sings "With a lit-tle bur-gla-ree! With cat-like tread Up-on our prey we steal; In si-lence dread Our cau-tious way we feel.", the lower "Ta-ran-ta-ra" and "ra, ra, ra!", over a two-staff piano part. A long pencil stroke runs down through the last system.
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el número 152 y el número de plancha de Chappell, 23731, al pie. La letra de ensayo E y "ff" marcan las dos líneas vocales: la de arriba canta "With a lit-tle bur-gla-ree! With cat-like tread Up-on our prey we steal; In si-lence dread Our cau-tious way we feel.", la de abajo "Ta-ran-ta-ra" y "ra, ra, ra!", sobre una parte de piano en dos pentagramas. Un largo trazo a lápiz baja por el último sistema.

caption.en: Page 152 of the later London printing of Chappell's vocal score, catalogued as about 1920, that our arrangement is read from: from letter E pirates and police sing together, fortissimo, to the final "Our cautious way we feel."
caption.es: La página 152 de la impresión londinense posterior de la partitura vocal de Chappell, catalogada como de hacia 1920, de la que está tomado nuestro arreglo: desde la letra E piratas y policías cantan juntos, fortissimo, hasta el último "Our cautious way we feel."

source: W. S. Gilbert and Arthur Sullivan, The Pirates of Penzance; or, The Slave of Duty, vocal score (London: Chappell & Co., plate 23731, catalogued [1920?]), Act II, No. 12, p. 152
